title: Launch checklist: hostname, zone and Workers Builds settings that live outside the repo and must be done by hand
evidence: wrangler.jsonc has no routes, custom_domain or workers_dev keys, so the custom domain must be attached in the dashboard. workers_list across all 8 Cloudflare accounts this session can reach (Zac@, Lsm@, AZ Turf, Cuka, Elk Mountain, Landmark, Screenguy, Skagway) finds no Worker named 'eastvalleynd-com'; the only ones are lostsearchmedia-com, stopdigitaldrift-com, fleet-auth-state and fleet-iframe. Cloudflare's docs say Custom Domains need an exact hostname match ('a Worker attached to example.com will not receive requests sent to www.example.com'), and a Custom Domain cannot be created on a hostname that already has a CNAME record. On wrangler dev, /?page_id=2919 (69 hits per the _redirects footer) and /?p=487 serve the homepage with 200, because _redirects cannot match query strings. dist/pagefind/ is produced only by the postbuild script (scripts/search-index.mjs), and npm runs prebuild/postbuild only for `npm run build`.
impact: If any of these is missed, eastvalleynd.com (apex) or http:// requests either fail or keep hitting the old WordPress host. Ranking signals then split across hosts, the page_id URL serves a duplicate homepage, and a build command of `astro build` deploys without the search index (search breaks).
fix: Cloudflare dashboard, no code. (1) Create or confirm the Worker 'eastvalleynd-com' (Workers Builds needs the name to match wrangler.jsonc). Connect it to main with Build command `npm run build` (not `astro build`) and Deploy command `npx wrangler deploy`. (2) Delete the existing www DNS record that points at WordPress, then add Custom Domain www.eastvalleynd.com to the Worker. (3) For the apex, add a proxied A record @ -> 192.0.2.0 and a Single Redirect rule 'root to www' (301, keep path and query). (4) Turn on SSL/TLS > Edge Certificates > Always Use HTTPS, and HSTS (start with a short max-age). (5) Add the 2 query-string Redirect Rules listed at the end of public/_redirects. (6) If the zone moves to Cloudflare nameservers, copy every existing record first (MX/SPF/DKIM for patientcare@ email, TXT verifications). (7) In Search Console, submit https://www.eastvalleynd.com/sitemap.xml and check how the property is verified: no page carries a google-site-verification meta, so a Yoast meta-tag verification would be lost.
verifyNote: Checked again and confirmed. wrangler.jsonc has no routes, custom_domain or workers_dev keys. workers_list across all 8 accounts finds no 'eastvalleynd-com' Worker; the only Workers are lostsearchmedia-com, stopdigitaldrift-com, fleet-auth-state and fleet-iframe. The Worker may still live in a client account this token cannot see, since the brief says pushes to main already build, so step (1) should read 'confirm' rather than 'create'. On wrangler dev, /?page_id=2919 and /?p=487 both return 200 with the homepage (187 KB), and _redirects only lists them as comments. package.json 'build' is plain 'astro build', and Pagefind and the stray-copy cleanup run only through npm's postbuild hook, so the build command must be 'npm run build'. CF docs agree that Workers Builds uses the package.json wrangler version, and that `npx wrangler` falls back to latest when none is set. No dist page has google-site-verification or msvalidate. Everything is dashboard work with no code change. High is right, because a missing apex or www hookup is a real launch failure.

title: 587 of the 646 legacy redirects return 404 when the URL is requested without its trailing slash
evidence: Every rule whose source ends in '/' (587 of them) was requested with the slash removed. All 587 returned 404, for example /pans-pandas, /skinpen, /sleep, /long-covid, /speciality_service/ozone-theraphy, /specialties/aesthetics-and-anti-aging and /evnd-treatment-center. The cause is the matcher in node_modules/miniflare/dist/src/workers/assets/assets.worker.js (scratchpad copy of the Cloudflare asset-worker): staticRedirectsMatcher looks up staticRules[pathname] by exact key, with no slash or case folding. Real pages are fine because auto-trailing-slash sends /about to /about/ with a 307. Redirect sources get no such treatment: they match only the exact string, and nothing falls back to them. On WordPress the slash-less form 301'd to the slash form and then redirected, so these inbound links worked before.
impact: Any backlink, bookmark, email link or hand-typed URL that left off the trailing slash on a retired URL turns into a 404 at launch. Those links worked on WordPress. The affected rules include the highest-traffic ones in the file, which is ordered by measured hits. Their link equity is lost.
fix: Content pipeline (extract/build_redirects.py, which generates public/_redirects and .htaccess): emit a second line for each slash-ending source without the slash, for example '/pans-pandas  /conditions/childhood-behavioral-disorders/pandas/  301'. That makes 1,233 static rules, under the 2,000 limit. Do not use a generic placeholder rule such as '/:slug /:slug/ 301'. Redirects run before assets, so it would also catch /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml.
verifyNote: Confirmed with every rule. I ran wrangler dev 4.148 against dist/ using the same assets config. All 646 sources return 301 when requested exactly as written. All 587 slash-ending sources return 404 with the slash removed, and no slashless variant exists in the file. Examples: /pans-pandas, /skinpen and /sleep return 404, while /about returns a 307 to /about/. In the asset-worker, staticRedirectsMatcher looks up staticRules[pathname] by exact key, and this is the same workers-shared code that production runs. The file has no dynamic rules and wrangler.jsonc has no Worker script, so nothing else catches these. The 59 non-slash rules (.html, .pdf, index.php) are not affected. No source shadows a real page. Severity is high rather than a blocker: the canonical slash forms that Google has indexed all work, so the losses are slashless backlinks, typed links and printed vanity links (e.g. /skinpen). The fix belongs in the content pipeline (extract/build_redirects.py). 646+587=1,233 static rules, under the 2,000 limit. I could not compare against the live WordPress site because the proxy blocks it.

title: 587 legacy redirects only match with a trailing slash; the slashless form returns 404
evidence: scratchpad/audit-build/scripts/redirects.mjs requested every rule against wrangler dev (same asset-worker code as production). All 646 rules work as written, but all 587 slash-terminated sources return 404 when requested without the slash. Examples: /speciality_service/ozone-theraphy (line 1, the top-traffic rule), /physicians/laura-kwiatkowski, /skinpen, /pans-pandas, /long-covid. Cloudflare _redirects matching is exact: the docs' own example `/trailing /trailing/ 301` shows the two forms are different paths. html_handling only adds a slash when a matching asset exists, which an old URL never has. WordPress used to 301 /foo to /foo/ before applying the old redirect.
impact: Every backlink, bookmark or typed URL to an old address without the slash, which used to reach the right page, becomes a 404 at launch. Link equity from those links is lost and visitors hit the 404 page.
fix: Generated side: extract/build_redirects.py should write a second line without the slash for each slash-terminated source (e.g. `/speciality_service/ozone-theraphy /ozone-therapy/ 301`). That makes 1,233 static rules, under the 2,000 limit. A splat rule cannot do this, because Cloudflare applies redirects before assets ('Redirects are always followed, regardless of whether or not an asset matches'). Optionally also write `/<page> /<page>/ 301` for the 235 live pages, which replaces the 307 described in a separate finding (about 1,470 rules in total).
verifyNote: Confirmed exhaustively. 646 rules parsed, 587 sources end in '/', and requesting all 587 without the slash on my own wrangler dev gave 587 x 404. The asset-worker code (workers-shared staticRedirectsMatcher) looks up staticRules[pathname] as an exact key, and html_handling only redirects when a real asset exists. I could not verify the claim that the old site matched slashless URLs, because www.eastvalleynd.com is blocked by the egress proxy. WordPress canonical redirects and the Redirection plugin's default 'ignore trailing slash' make it likely. Most backlinks use the slash form that WordPress emitted, so medium is the upper bound. The generated-side fix (duplicate the lines in extract/build_redirects.py, about 1,233 static rules, under the 2,000 limit) is correct.

title: Favicon is a 750x300 wide logo; no square icon and no /favicon.ico
evidence: src/layouts/Base.astro:147 `<link rel="icon" href="/assets/evnd-logo.png" />`. `file` reports public/assets/evnd-logo.png as 750 x 300 PNG. Requesting /favicon.ico on wrangler dev returns 404 (the 74 KB 404 page). The source has no apple-touch-icon and no square icon.
impact: Google requires a square (1:1) favicon of at least 8x8 px (more than 48x48 recommended) to show it next to search results. A 2.5:1 logo is likely to be replaced by a generic globe icon, the result looks less trustworthy than the WordPress listing, and browser tabs show a squashed logo. Every browser's automatic /favicon.ico request also downloads the full 404 page.
fix: Hand-kept. Add a square icon set (e.g. 48/96/192 px PNG or SVG, a /favicon.ico, and a 180 px apple-touch-icon) under public/ and reference it in src/layouts/Base.astro.
verifyNote: Confirmed. Base.astro:147 is the only icon link and points to /assets/evnd-logo.png, a 750x300 PNG. There is no apple-touch-icon, manifest or square icon, and /favicon.ico returns 404 (the 74 KB 404 page). Google requires a 1:1 favicon, so the SERP icon will likely fall back to a generic one, which is a visible regression from WordPress. One overstatement: Chrome and Firefox do not request /favicon.ico when a rel=icon link is present, so not 'every browser' downloads the 404. Some clients and crawlers do. Fix in hand-kept files: public/ plus Base.astro.

title: Three pairs of identical pages are both indexable, self-canonical and in sitemap.xml (plus one near-duplicate pair)
evidence: Shingle similarity (Jaccard), title, H1 and description all identical in each pair: /allergies/ vs /conditions/allergies/ (J=0.92, 'Allergies — EVND', same description); /infertility/ vs /conditions/infertility/ (J=0.93, 'Infertility — EVND'); /suffering-from-childhood-allergies/ vs /conditions/childhood-medical-disorders/childhood-allergies/ (J=0.93, same description). Cause: one WordPress post feeds two collections. src/content/blog/allergies.md and src/content/pages/conditions-allergies.md both have sourceUrl '/allergies/'; the same holds for /infertility/ and /suffering-from-childhood-allergies/. Near-duplicate: /what-causes-vaginal-infections/ vs /conditions/womens-health/vaginal-infections/ (J=0.63; 83% of one is in the other). BlogPost.astro has no canonical or noindex support, so src/data/duplicate-pages.ts cannot reach the blog copies. public/_redirects already sends /rhinitis/ to /allergies/.
impact: Google picks one URL of each pair itself, ranking signals split, and duplicate SERP entries are possible for core condition terms (allergies, infertility). Both copies are announced in the sitemap at launch.
fix: Permanent fix in the pipeline (extract/build_blog.py, build_sitemap_xml.py): keep the condition page (it is in the nav; /conditions/infertility/ has 251 inbound links); 301 /allergies/, /infertility/ and /suffering-from-childhood-allergies/ to it in public/_redirects; repoint /rhinitis/ straight to the kept page; drop the blog copy from src/content/blog and sitemap.xml. Interim hand fix: make BlogPost.astro read src/data/duplicate-pages.ts and pass canonicalPath + noindex to Base, as ContentPage.astro does, and add the 3 (or 4) blog slugs there.
verifyNote: Confirmed. Shingle Jaccard is 0.92-0.93 for /allergies/ vs /conditions/allergies/, /infertility/ vs /conditions/infertility/, and /suffering-from-childhood-allergies/ vs the childhood-allergies condition page. In each pair both pages have the same description, no robots meta, a self canonical and a sitemap entry. The blog and pages .md files share the same sourceUrl. BlogPost.astro never reads duplicate-pages.ts (only ContentPage does, via isDuplicate), and _redirects has /rhinitis/ -> /allergies/. The vaginal-infections pair scores J=0.71, but it comes from two separate WordPress pages (/condition/vaginal-infections/ and /what-causes-vaginal-infections/), so it predates the migration. Downgraded to medium: Google folds exact duplicates into one URL, so this splits signals but does not drop pages, and /allergies/ and /infertility/ are the old WordPress URLs and keep their history. The fix (pipeline 301 plus interim noindex/canonical support in BlogPost.astro) is right.

title: Yoast sitemap URLs that Google already knows return 404
evidence: The old site used Yoast (src/layouts/Base.astro line 95: 'the old site had this via Yoast'). /sitemap_index.xml, /page-sitemap.xml, /post-sitemap.xml, /category-sitemap.xml and /author-sitemap.xml all return 404. No _redirects rule covers them.

The cost is a Search Console sitemap error plus a small discovery delay, not lost rankings. A redirect from sitemap_index.xml to /sitemap.xml is a cheap tidy-up (pipeline _redirects).
